title: At APEC in Shenzhen, Sheinbaum Says No Nation Can Grow at Another’s Expense; the Key Is Shared Prosperity
author: Angeles Cruz Martínez
content:
_This article by[Angeles Cruz
Martínez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Angeles%20Cruz%20Mart%C3%ADnez%2C%20enviada.%20Shenzhen),
special correspondent in Shenzhen, originally appeared in the [November 16,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/16/politica/bienestar-y-
prosperidad-debe-ser-una-conquista-compartida-sheinbaum-ante-lideres-
empresariales-de-apec), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Shenzhen.** A nation’s development and prosperity cannot come at the expense
of another’s decline or stagnation. There must be cooperation to achieve
shared prosperity, President Claudia Sheinbaum said at the [Asia-Pacific
Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO
Summit](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/16/politica/sheinbaum-
participara-en-la-cumbre-de-lideres-empresariales-de-apec-este-martes-en-
china).

Mexico offers certainty and a long-term vision through Plan México, alongside
the country’s privileged position and an economy integrated into the world’s
main markets. She stressed that the most important asset for this is the human
talent available.

In a measured and firm address, the president outlined the guidelines of Plan
México, the country’s development model, which seeks people’s well-being.

And that is because the economy must serve the population, not the other way
around, she emphasized.

She explained that in Mexico we are demonstrating that the path can be
different and called for “prosperity to be a shared achievement.”

The president addressed guests from the [21 APEC
economies](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/16/politica/sheinbaum-
lleva-a-china-la-voz-de-un-mexico-soberano-afirma-rosa-icela-rodriguez) and 13
outside economies, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany and
Switzerland, participating in the summit.

She was welcomed by Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the
Promotion of International Trade and of the summit, who introduced her. The
president began her address with the support of several slides showing the
results of social programs and infrastructure investment projects.

## Certainty for Global Value Chains

Sheinbaum spoke about the benefits of Plan México, including shared
prosperity, energy and food sovereignty, public, private and mixed investment
in infrastructure, and environmental responsibility in the face of climate
change.

“We are building our own model, rooted in our own history. It began with Plan
México, which is the decision to turn our capabilities, resources, strategic
position and talent into engines of development with sovereignty and social
justice,” the president said.

![Claudia Sheinbaum speaks with a reporter in a hallway at the APEC CEO
Summit.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/sheinbaum-
apec-shared-prosperity-photo-1.webp)Photo: Presidency.

At the same time, she noted that in Mexico, **the minimum wage increased 154
percent in real terms** over the past eight years; 42 million people receive
direct transfers through a historic investment of one trillion pesos through
Banco del Bienestar, and more than 17 million people have left poverty from
2018 to 2026.

Citing former president Benito Juárez’s statement that “respect for the rights
of others is peace,” Sheinbaum Pardo advocated extending that principle to the
economic sphere as well, stating that “the development of one nation must not
mean the decline or stagnation of another, but rather cooperation for shared
prosperity. [In an interconnected
world](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/16/economia/de-importancia-
revolucionaria-la-reunion-de-los-presidentes-xi-putin-y-trump), cooperation,
trade, investment and the exchange of knowledge must strengthen the
capabilities of all economies, of all nations. Development reaches its true
greatness when it becomes well-being for everyone.”

Mexico is demonstrating that there is “another way to promote and understand
development. One in which the strength of an economy is measured not only by
how much it produces, but by the well-being it generates.”

## Fifth-Ranked Economy in Foreign Direct Investment

Sheinbaum stressed that Mexico is among the five countries producing the most
engineers in the world and has public universities: “We have the capacity to
participate in major global value chains, but also to innovate and build
strategic industries.”

At the same time, she said, we are “promoting industrial and services
investment through incentives, certainty, administrative simplification and
new development hubs linked to each territory’s productive strengths. This
allows us to be the fifth-ranked economy in foreign direct investment
worldwide.”

![Claudia Sheinbaum stands among applauding delegates at the APEC CEO Summit
in Shenzhen.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/sheinbaum-apec-shared-prosperity-photo-2.webp)Photo:
Presidency.

She added that progress is being made along a path for Mexico to produce more
and better; import technology; incorporate technology; generate greater added
value; and develop its own industrial and scientific capabilities.

She said a process is underway to expand electricity generation by **32
thousand megawatts** , with a growing share of renewable energy, representing
an investment of 42 trillion dollars in generation, 17 trillion dollars in
transmission and distribution, and 8 trillion dollars in gas pipelines.

Mexico’s privileged geographic position helps guarantee that the conditions
for investment and long-term certainty exist, which is why “our model is not a
copy of an imported formula; it is born of our history and our own
experience.”

Plan México has a **humanist vision, with the economy serving people** and not
people serving the economy, because “for decades it was held that the wealth
of a few had to grow first and would then reach the rest of society,” the
president said.
